waypoints.name: No. 19 Konigstrasse, Hamburg
waypoints.notes: The domestic starting point in old Hamburg is given precisely by street, not by modern parcel.

waypoints.name: Altona station
waypoints.notes: The rail departure point for Kiel.

waypoints.name: Faroe waters
waypoints.notes: The book gives the North Atlantic progression; this waypoint shapes the sea route.

waypoints.name: Cape Portland approach
waypoints.notes: Cape Portland is treated as the south-Iceland approach named in the voyage.

waypoints.name: Hvalfjord crossing
waypoints.notes: The exact ferry point is not fixed in the text; the app marks the fjord crossing itself.

waypoints.name: Krosolbt
waypoints.notes: A named stage in the translation. Position is inferred to preserve the coastal march.

waypoints.name: Stapi
waypoints.notes: Modern Arnarstapi, the last settlement before the mountain.

waypoints.name: Scartaris crater
waypoints.notes: The crater is selected by the shadow of Scartaris before the kalends of July.

waypoints.name: Crater bottom at sea level
waypoints.notes: The book describes the vertical tube ending near sea level after the descent from Snaefell.

waypoints.name: Steep ESE lava staircase
waypoints.notes: By the first underground halt the party is about 10,000 feet below sea level, still in the inclined lava gallery.

waypoints.name: Eastern / western gallery fork
waypoints.notes: At the end of the chimney the party finds two dark narrow roads and chooses the eastern one by chance.

waypoints.name: Eastern blind alley
waypoints.notes: The mistaken eastern tunnel levels out, rises slightly, crosses fossiliferous beds, and ends at a wall.

waypoints.name: Western granite fissure
waypoints.notes: The second gallery is a winding fissure in primitive rock, chosen after returning from the blind alley.

waypoints.name: Hansbach
waypoints.notes: Hans opens the rock and discovers the stream that saves the expedition.

waypoints.name: Sixteen leagues deep
waypoints.notes: The Professor states they are 85 leagues from Snaefell and 16 leagues deep.

waypoints.name: Liedenbrock Sea
waypoints.notes: The underground sea is fictional; shape and position are cinematic.

waypoints.name: Axel Island
waypoints.notes: The Professor counts 270 leagues of sea by the island/geyser stage.

waypoints.name: Storm landfall
waypoints.notes: After the electric storm, the Professor estimates another 300 leagues of drift.

waypoints.name: Cape Saknussemm
waypoints.notes: The name marks the rediscovered Saknussemm route after the storm has reversed the party.

waypoints.name: Volcanic conduit
waypoints.notes: The explosion opens a water-driven descent and then a violent upward volcanic transport.

waypoints.name: Stromboli
waypoints.notes: The party emerges on Stromboli, more than two thousand miles from Snaefell by the text.

waypoints.name: San Vicenzo port
waypoints.notes: The book names the port reached after leaving the grove on Stromboli.

paths.title: Hamburg departure
paths.notes: The party leaves Hamburg for the Altona railway station.

sourceRefs.label: Pack trunks and depart for Copenhagen route

paths.title: Rail to Kiel
paths.notes: Surface route distance is calculated from modern coordinates.

paths.title: Belt steamer
paths.notes: The sea crossing links the German and Danish rail portions.

paths.title: Rail across Zealand
paths.notes: The last rail segment before the Copenhagen preparations.

paths.title: Out through the Sound
paths.notes: The route follows the Sound and the Danish coast before entering the North Sea.

paths.title: North Sea crossing
paths.notes: Cinematic leg through the North Atlantic corridor described in the voyage.

paths.title: Toward Iceland
paths.notes: The text names Cape Portland before the approach to Faxa Bay.

paths.title: Faxa Bay arrival
paths.notes: The final sea approach to Reykjavik.

paths.title: First Iceland stage
paths.notes: Hans leads the party out of Reykjavik toward the coast road.

sourceRefs.label: Two hours from Reykjavik to Gufunes

paths.title: Around Kolla fiord
paths.notes: The book counts four Icelandic miles, or twenty-four English miles, by this stage.

sourceRefs.label: Four Icelandic miles by late afternoon

paths.title: Hvalfjord ferry
paths.notes: The fjord is described as at least three English miles wide and crossed by raft/boat at slack tide.

sourceRefs.label: Hvalfjord ferry waits for the tide

paths.title: Coastal barrens
paths.notes: A long inferred coastal stage preserving the novel itinerary toward the Snaefellsnes peninsula.

paths.title: Hraun and hot springs
paths.notes: The text notes hardened lava, bogs, small lakes, and the white twin peaks ahead.

sourceRefs.label: Hraun and first close views of Snaefell

paths.title: To Stapi
paths.notes: The horses stop at the rector blacksmith house at Stapi.

paths.title: Assault on Snaefell
paths.notes: Hans leads the ascent over basalt, peat, and loose rock.

sourceRefs.label: Stapi to the base of Snaefell

paths.title: Scartaris crater
paths.notes: The party reaches the crater indicated by the shadow of Scartaris.

paths.title: Vertical descent
paths.notes: Snaefell is given as five thousand feet high; the tube reaches about sea level.

sourceRefs.label: Barometer shows the bottom at sea level

paths.title: Inclined lava staircase
paths.notes: After the sea-level crater floor, the route becomes a sloped natural staircase rather than a vertical shaft.

sourceRefs.label: Inclined lava gallery reaches 10,000 feet below sea level

paths.title: End of the chimney
paths.notes: They continue down the gently sloped lava staircase until Hans stops at the intersection of two roads.

sourceRefs.label: Intersection of the eastern and western roads

paths.title: Mistaken eastern gallery
paths.notes: Liedenbrock chooses the eastern tunnel by chance; it becomes nearly horizontal, then rises, leaves the lava path, and ends at a blind wall.

sourceRefs.label: The blind alley proves the road was wrong

paths.title: Three-day return to the fork
paths.notes: With water exhausted, the party retraces the mistaken eastern gallery back to the cross roads before trying the other branch.

sourceRefs.label: Return from the dry eastern gallery to the cross roads

paths.title: Western gallery descent
paths.notes: The western fissure descends through primitive rock in a maze of windings rather than dropping straight down.

sourceRefs.label: Proposal to try the western tunnel
Primitive rocks and winding granite fissure

paths.title: Hansbach
paths.notes: Hans leads them down a passage inclining two feet in seven; after about a mile and a quarter plus another half league they hear the buried torrent.

sourceRefs.label: Water discovered down the inclined passage

paths.title: Eighty-five leagues from Snaefell
paths.notes: The Hansbach first follows spiral curves down a fault, then a south-easterly slope; by chapter XXV the Professor reckons 85 leagues from Snaefell and 16 leagues deep.

paths.title: Axel separates
paths.notes: Axel loses the party in the labyrinth while the stream and galleries complicate the route.

sourceRefs.label: Lost in the bowels of the earth

paths.title: Whispering gallery
paths.notes: The concave gallery carries voices across the rock and guides Axel back.

paths.title: Thalatta
paths.notes: Axel falls into a shaft and wakes near the shore of the underground sea.

paths.title: Raft built on the shore
paths.notes: Hans builds the raft for the voyage across the Mare Internum.

paths.title: Across Liedenbrock Sea
paths.notes: The Professor estimates 270 leagues of sea by the Axel Island and geyser stage.

paths.title: Electric storm drift
paths.notes: After the storm, the Professor estimates at least 80 leagues per day over four days.

paths.title: Back to Saknussemm route
paths.notes: The party discovers it has been carried back toward the northern route and Cape Saknussemm.

paths.title: Fossil forest
paths.notes: The forest sequence is staged as a side excursion near the second shore.

paths.title: Blocked passage
paths.notes: A granite block prevents progress and prompts the blasting plan.

paths.title: Explosion and rush below
paths.notes: The route becomes a violent water and lava conduit after the explosion.

paths.title: Shot out at Stromboli
paths.notes: The book gives the final displacement as more than two thousand miles from Snaefell; the visible curve is cinematic.

sourceRefs.label: Stromboli exit; more than two thousand miles from Snaefell

paths.title: To San Vicenzo
paths.notes: The party walks from the grove toward the small port on Stromboli.

sourceRefs.label: One hour to the port of San Vicenzo
